cleaving_frame: Supply vs Demand / Scarcity vs Abundance
description: The problem involves finite resources (capital, time, talent, attention) that must be distributed across competing uses. The structural question is where to deploy scarce resources for maximum return.
detect_when: Multiple uses compete for the same pool of resources (capital, time, headcount, attention)
Choosing one option means forgoing another — the displaced alternative matters
The constraint is how much is available, not what to do with it
A continuation or default path is being treated as free when it consumes real resources
coverage_signals: The answer explicitly identifies what is being given up (the displaced alternative)
The answer compares marginal returns across options, not just absolute returns
The answer sizes the resource constraint and tests whether it binds
The answer distinguishes between the vital few uses and the trivial many
materiality_test: Would reallocating the same resources differently change the recommended outcome?
reasoning_demanded: opportunity cost analysis, marginal return comparison, constraint sizing
curation_note: All six models validated against canonical articles. Opportunity-cost provides the 'compared to what?' forcing function. Comparative-advantage directs effort to highest input-to-output ratio. Trade-offs addresses balancing competing demands under scarcity. Pareto-principle identifies the vital few vs trivial many. Prioritization provides the exclusion discipline. Optimization-theory frames constrained maximization. Together they cover the full resource allocation reasoning surface.

detect_when.note: Detection conditions drawn from opportunity-cost ('compared to what?', displaced alternatives), trade-offs (forces constantly conflicting, scarce resources), and prioritization (what to do and what not to do). The continuation-as-free trigger from opportunity-cost's 'sponge vs sieve' metaphor.

coverage_signals.note: Signals map to source material: displaced alternative from opportunity-cost, marginal return comparison from trade-offs CBA framework, constraint sizing from optimization-theory's constrained optimization, vital few from pareto-principle.

models.note: All six models have explicit resource allocation activation in their canonical articles. Opportunity-cost and trade-offs are the primary pair. Pareto and prioritization reinforce the 'what not to do' discipline. Comparative-advantage and optimization-theory round out the structural reasoning.
